NB: Not proofread yet 😉 [████] Danish AI art will disrupt international politics Can artificial intelligence create a voice for the opinions and voices that have difficulty getting through, thereby contributing to a deeper democratic debate? This is what the Danish art research project "Automatic Uprisings" now tries to answer through the creation of AI art. Novo Nordisk Foundation has awarded a Mads Øvlisen PhD scholarship of 2 million DKK to the artistic researcher Asker Bryld Staunæs, who in collaboration with Kunsthal Aarhus and Aarhus University will construct an international network of synthetic parties and virtual politicians through art and research. The lost voices Who speaks on behalf of couch voters? How do the smaller parties get through the media wall and be heard? And how will it affect the political debate if these voices become more distinct? Through the project "The Synthetic Party" the AI-based politician "Leader Lars" has the past year given voice to those opinions that rarely find their way into the political debate. "The Synthetic Party's" opinions and policies are AI-generated from the micro-parties that are not eligible for election in Denmark, with the purpose of giving a voice to approximately 20 % of Danes who do not vote. "Automatic Uprisings seeks to explore the potential of artificial intelligence to visualize ideas about social uprisings. The project challenges existing notions of democratic participation and questions parliamentarism’s capacity to include all voices in society. With 'The Synthetic Party' we have constructed a platform where a global audience has interacted with visions from Danish couch voters and smaller parties through our virtual politician, 'Leader Lars'. Now we are ready to conceptualize this format at a global level as a "synthetic international". Our vision is to build a network of synthetic parties and virtual politicians across different cultures. Through algorithmic presentation, we will activate hitherto unrecognized forms of democratic participation," says Asker Bryld Staunæs. To illustrate the differences between his research and existing initiatives regarding AI and democracy, Staunæs adds, that where "e.g. the EU narrowly focuses on regulation of artificial intelligence and among other things underestimates political campaigns with AI as misinformation or influence on elections, a 'synthetic international' can ask whether AI technology can strengthen competencies for democratic participation and digital citizenship." An important contribution to the debate It is the Novo Nordisk Foundation that has awarded the Mads Øvlisen PhD scholarship of 2 million DKK to Asker’s artistic research, which should contribute to the debate about AI’s impact on democracy and the international political conversation. ”XXXXX – quote with justification for the award,” says XXXX from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. An important contribution to the debate AI is becoming a bigger and bigger part of our everyday lives, and with the release of ChatGPT and several of tech-world’s biggest icons distancing themselves from AI development, the debate is hotter than ever.
